campus: Campus of Economics and Law, Via dei Caniana 2, Bergamo
programme_name_history: The current official English name is Economics & Finance (also written Economics and Finance or abbreviated EF). It is a separate LM-16 programme from Economics and Data Analysis.
admission_type: Open access, with committee verification of curricular requirements and adequacy of preparation. An online oral interview is mandatory for international applicants using the foreign-qualification pre-assessment route and for candidates who only partially meet curricular requirements; certain Italian-degree candidates are admitted directly according to degree grade.
academic_requirements: A three-year bachelor's degree or equivalent foreign qualification is required. Holders of an Italian degree in L-7, L-8, L-9, L-14, L-16, L-18, L-20, L-30, L-31, L-33, L-35, L-36, L-37 or L-41 (or an equivalent former DM 509/99 class) are admitted directly if their final grade is above 81/110 and otherwise undergo an interview. Holders of other Italian degree classes must meet the specified mathematics, statistics, economics and computing requirements and are likewise admitted directly above 81/110 or interviewed at 81/110 or below. Candidates not yet graduated from an Italian university are assessed under these criteria if their weighted bachelor's average is above 22/30. International applicants undergo CV and qualification evaluation plus a mandatory interview.

curricular_requirements_cfu.applicants_from_listed_italian_degree_cl: No additional subject-credit breakdown is stated; direct admission requires a final grade above 81/110, while a grade of 81/110 or below triggers an interview.
applicants_from_other_italian_degree_cla: 6 ECTS in mathematics: MAT/01-MAT/09 or SECS-S/06
6 ECTS in statistics: SECS-S/01-SECS-S/05 or SECS-P/05
12 ECTS in economics: SECS-P/01-SECS-P/03 or SECS-P/06
ECDL computer-skills certification, or 3 ECTS in INF/01 or ING-INF/05, or an equivalent diploma

entry_exam_or_test: No competitive entrance test is stated. Where required, admission depends on an individual online oral interview covering economics, mathematics, statistics and finance: rational consumer choice; information economics; foundations and applications of one-variable calculus; descriptive statistics; probability; and capital structure under perfect-markets, tax and organization theories.
interview_required: Mandatory for international candidates applying for a visa and/or holding a foreign qualification through online pre-assessment, and for candidates who only partially meet curricular requirements. Italian-degree applicants in the listed/eligible routes are interviewed when the degree grade is 81/110 or below; qualifying applicants above 81/110 are admitted directly.
selection_scoring: No competitive ranking score or numerical interview threshold is published on the programme admission page. For applicable Italian qualifications, a degree grade above 81/110 gives direct admission; 81/110 or below leads to interview. For not-yet-graduated Italian-university candidates, the published weighted-average condition is above 22/30.
degree_completion_deadline: Pre-enrolment with reserve may be permitted if curricular requirements are already met by the relevant pre-enrolment deadline. Under the central 2026/27 master's rules, the bachelor's degree must be completed by the extraordinary March/April 2027 graduation session.
application_channel: International candidates with qualifications obtained abroad use the University of Bergamo online pre-evaluation route and DreamApply; eligible non-EU visa applicants subsequently complete Universitaly pre-enrolment. Italian and EU candidates follow the UniBG master's pre-enrolment/enrolment procedure through the online student services.
language_requirements: English proficiency at CEFR B2 or equivalent is required. The programme states that B2 equivalence may be demonstrated by at least 6 ECTS of English during the bachelor's degree, at least six months living or working in an English-speaking country, or at least six months attending a university course abroad taught in English. The international online application route accepts the listed B2 certificates or an eligible medium-of-instruction certificate.
accepted_english_certificates: Cambridge First Certificate/FCE: grades B or C
Pearson Test of English General: Level 3
TIE: minimum B2 in both oral and written tests
ESB ESOL International: minimum Pass with Merit
language_waiver_conditions: For international pre-evaluation, a medium-of-instruction certificate issued by the registrar or international office is accepted if the completed degree was taught entirely in English; unofficial certificates and self-declarations are not accepted. Native English-speaking applicants are exempt from both an English certificate and medium-of-instruction certificate. The programme also recognizes the B2-equivalent experience/credit routes described in language_requirements.
results_notification_date: No separate results-publication date stated for the standard open-access pre-enrolment rounds [uncertain]
required_documents: Bachelor degree certificate translated into English or Italian
Official academic transcript for the last three/four years translated into English or Italian, or Diploma Supplement
Major-area form/course descriptions listing relevant contents, themes, aims and objectives
English-language evidence: accepted B2 certificate or qualifying medium-of-instruction certificate
Valid passport showing full name, photograph and signature
course_descriptions_required: Yes. International online pre-evaluation requires the Economics and Finance major-area form/course descriptions covering relevant contents, themes, aims and objectives.
application_fee: EUR 30 pre-evaluation fee for the 2026/27 non-EU online pre-evaluation route.
pre_enrolment_fee: EUR 52 for each selected master's programme; non-refundable and payable by eligible applicants.
enrolment_deposit: EUR 156 one-time, non-refundable enrolment fee payable on arrival in Italy, as stated on the official DreamApply programme record.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.unibg.it/studiare/iscriversi/tasse-e-agevolazioni/contribuzione-studentesca — official 2026/27 student-contribution page. The official DreamApply record summarizes tuition as EUR 0-400 for the first instalment and EUR 0-1,700 for the second, depending on family income; the central current-cycle contribution page should prevail.
tuition_income_linked: Yes. For 2026/27, the regional tax is EUR 130-190 by ISEEU band and the all-inclusive contribution varies by ISEEU, programme area, enrolment year and full-/part-time status. International students may use equivalent ISEEU documentation.

source_quotes.quote: The admission to the master degree in Economics and Finance (EF) ... is subject to an assessment process to certify the suitability of the candidate.
Direct admission with a degree grade greater than 81/110.
6 ECTS for the mathematics area ... 6 ECTS for the statistics area ... 12 ECTS for the economic area
For international students, the assessment will be done through an interview.
At least 1 reference(s) should be provided.
From November 24th 2025 to January 15th 2026: prospective students can apply
From January 1st 2026 to January 31st 2026: prospective students can apply

uncertainty_notes: The programme-specific admissions page and central UniBG pages contain current 2026/27 links and deadlines. The DreamApply record displays four ended 2026/27 application buttons without dates, so the exact non-EU dates and result dates are taken from UniBG's central 2026/27 international pre-evaluation page. The interview language is not explicitly identified on the programme admission page. Standard EU/Italian deadlines and early non-EU visa pre-evaluation deadlines represent different routes and should not be treated as interchangeable. Economics & Finance is not Economics and Data Analysis.
source_access_status: Official UNIBG sources only. The ls-ef.unibg.it programme admissions page and apply.unibg.it programme record were directly accessible through indexed official-page content; central en.unibg.it pages were available through current official search indexing, although some direct fetches returned HTTP 403.
